issues.legal_issue: The power to exempt excess vacant land from acquisition does not include the power to permit its transfer.
material_facts: A landholder held vacant urban land in excess of the ceiling limit, with a factory operating on a small portion of the land.
The landholder sought exemption and permission to sell the excess vacant land to another party, relying principally on business losses and indebtedness.
The State Government granted exemption and permission to sell the land under its exemption power.
issues.conclusion: The exemption power does not authorize the State Government to permit the sale of excess vacant land; the landholder may not transfer such land unless the applicable transfer provisions permit it.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 20(1)(a) and 20(1)(b) of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 permit exemption from Chapter III for purposes connected with use of the land, not for its transfer. The Act regulates transfers separately in Sections 26 to 28, and its scheme does not permit transfer of excess vacant land without a building except as those provisions allow. Permitting sale based on indebtedness would conflict with the Act’s objectives of preventing concentration, speculation and profiteering and promoting equitable distribution for the common good. Maharao Sahib Shri Bhim Singhji v. Union of India, [1981] 1 SCC 166, was relied on concerning Section 27; Thakorbhai Dajibhai Desai v. State of Gujarat, AIR 1980 Guj. 189, was overruled insofar as it treated indebtedness as a basis for exemption. The Court also reasoned that a debtor/non-debtor distinction used to permit such sales would be irrational and violate Article 14.

predicates.excess_land_transfer_exemption_dispute: The proceeding challenges a government exemption and permission intended to enable transfer of excess vacant land.
predicates.excess_vacant_land_was_held: A landholder held vacant urban land exceeding the applicable ceiling.
predicates.exemption_order_was_used_to_permit_sale: The government relied on an exemption order to permit the landholder to sell the excess vacant land.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns an exemption used to enable sale of excess vacant urban land, and the landholder held such land, the State cannot permit the transfer through that exemption.

issues.legal_issue: A government permission to sell excess vacant land issued without authority under the governing transfer rules is void, and a sale deed made under that permission is invalid and inoperative.
material_facts: The State Government issued orders exempting excess vacant land and permitting its sale to a purchaser.
The landholder then executed a sale deed for the land in reliance on those orders.
The orders and the sale deed were challenged in proceedings concerning the legality of the exemption and transfer.
issues.conclusion: The exemption and sale-permission orders were void ab initio, and the sale deed was invalid and inoperative because the landholder had no legal right to transfer the land to the purchaser.
issues.legal_principle: Because Sections 20(1)(a) and 20(1)(b) do not authorize exemption for the purpose of transferring excess vacant land, an order purporting to permit such a sale is without jurisdiction. A sale deed executed on the basis of that unauthorized permission cannot give effect to a transfer the landholder had no legal right to make. The Court relied on the statutory scheme governing exemptions and transfers in Sections 20 and 26 to 28 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976.

predicates.appeal_challenges_exemption_and_sale: The proceeding challenges both a government exemption or sale permission and a transfer made under it.
predicates.government_order_purported_to_permit_sal: The government issued an order purporting to allow the sale of excess vacant land.
predicates.sale_deed_was_executed_under_that_permis: The landholder executed a sale deed in reliance on the government’s permission.

issues.definition: When a challenged order purports to permit sale of excess vacant land and a sale deed is executed under that permission, the unauthorized permission is void and the deed is invalid and inoperative.
